$comment: How good the output has to be, per operation, for the models the app actually serves. The floor in scripts/quality-gate.mjs says 'not terrible'; this says 'not worse than it was'. Written by `npm run llm:quality:baseline -- --reason "..."` from the baked scorecard (src/lib/llm/quality-scores.ts) and read on every CI run by scripts/quality-gate.mjs. Every move is recorded in test-llm/quality/CHANGELOG.md.
acceptedReason: seeded from the 2026-07-07 matrix bake — the numbers the app has been shipping with, recorded so the next bake can be compared to them instead of only to the 6.5 floor
$thresholds: maxDrop is per cell: half a point is judge variance (the same variance the 6.5 floor allows for), so a full point is the smallest drop that means something changed. maxMeanDrop is the answer to the failure the per-cell rule cannot see — every operation losing 0.9 and passing. The two together are what makes a slow degradation a red build rather than something a marketer notices first.
